{"additions":26,"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjE2MTE1MTA=","is_bot":false,"login":"williammartin","name":"William Martin"},"baseRefName":"trunk","body":" ### Description On every invocation, `gh` registers a cobra command for each installed extension. While registering, it decides whether to record telemetry for that extension: only official GitHub-owned extensions (`github/gh-aw`, `github/gh-stack`, `cli/gh-webhook`) are allowed to. That check called `ext.Owner()` for every installed extension before comparing names. For extensions installed with `gh extension install` from a repository without release binaries (script extensions), the extension is a git clone, and `Owner()` resolves the owner by running `git config remote.origin.url`. That meant one `git` process per script extension on every `gh` command, including `gh --version` and `gh help`. This change makes `extensions.IsOfficial` take the extension and resolve the owner only after the name matches an official extension. Third-party extensions, which are nearly all of them, never trigger the owner lookup. ### How did you test this change? I built `gh` from `trunk` and from this branch, then set up an isolated `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `GH_CONFIG_DIR` containing 5 git-cloned script extensions (`gh-one` to `gh-five`, each with an `origin` remote of `https://github.com/someone/gh-.git`). `gh extension list` showed all five as `someone/gh-*`. I then ran hyperfine on `gh --version` (macOS, Apple M4 Max): ``` $ hyperfine -N --warmup 10 --runs 100 -n "before (trunk)" "gh-before --version" -n "after (this PR)" "gh-after --version" Benchmark 1: before (trunk) Time (mean ± σ): 46.3 ms ± 3.5 ms [User: 27.0 ms, System: 18.0 ms] Range (min … max): 42.3 ms … 63.4 ms 100 runs Benchmark 2: after (this PR) Time (mean ± σ): 20.6 ms ± 1.4 ms [User: 17.6 ms, System: 6.3 ms] Range (min … max): 18.7 ms … 27.9 ms 100 runs Summary after (this PR) ran 2.24 ± 0.23 times faster than before (trunk) ``` That is about 5 ms saved per script extension per invocation. With no extensions installed I measured about 22 ms for both builds, so this change returns startup to roughly the no-extension baseline. To check that telemetry gating is unchanged, I added a git-cloned `gh-stack` extension with an `origin` of `https://github.com/github/gh-stack.git` and ran both builds with `GH_TELEMETRY=log`: - `gh stack` logged a `command_invocation` event with `"command": "gh stack"` on both builds. - `gh one` (a third-party extension) logged no command event on either build. ### Key points - `IsOfficial` now takes an `extensions.Extension` instead of `(name, owner string)`. It had a single caller, and passing the extension lets the function decide whether the owner is needed, so callers can't accidentally resolve it eagerly again. - The owner is looked up at most once, because official extension names are unique in the registry. - Binary extensions (with a `manifest.yml`) and local extensions were cheap before (a small file read, or nothing), so users with only those see no measurable change. The gain is specific to git-installed script extensions and grows with how many are installed. ### Notes for reviewers Start with `pkg/extensions/official.go`. The existing `TestIsOfficial` cases are kept unchanged in behavior and now use `ExtensionMock`. `TestIsOfficial_DoesNotResolveOwnerForUnofficialNames` asserts that `Owner()` is not called for a non-official name. ### Authorship and follow-up Who wrote this: - [ ] A human wrote it. - [x] An agent wrote it under close human direction. - [ ] An agent wrote it independently, and no human has guided the implementation beyond the initial prompt.
